newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals firm, focus on dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals firm, focus on dlr/yen.

text.p: * Regional currencies are mostly bound in narrow ranges with the focus mainly on the dollar's fall against the yen to 111.80 yen in the late morning.
* The Thai baht is firmer on back of dollar/yen weakness. Offshore market remains short of baht funds.
* The ringgit is range bound despite the weaker dollar. Some ringgit selling seen from U.S. funds but likely to stay within 2.5150 and 2.5080 for the day.
* Singapore dollar firmer on back of weak dollar/yen. Seen testing upside at 1.4260.
* Indonesian rupiah steady after elections.
Asian regional currencies were mostly steady, trapped in narrow ranges in late Monday morning trade with the markets focus on the sharply weaker dollar/yen.
The dollar plunged below 112 yen level to touch 111.80, its lowest level since November 25, 1996, in late morning trade on bearish dollar sentiment and speculative sales.
The Thai baht firmed against the dollar in onshore and offshore markets on back of the dollar's weakness abroad, dealers said.

The baht was traded at 23.90/24.00 to the dollar early in the offshore market compared with 23.950/24.050 late on Friday. The baht was quoted at 25.740/25.760 in domestic market against 25.815/25.825 late on Friday.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.75.
A dealer in Singapore said the market was still very short of baht funds almost a month after the speculative attacks on the baht and he expected the baht to range between 23.75 to 24.40.
Dealers said strong demand for baht among offshore parties also triggered sustained foreign selling of dollars for baht.
The Malaysian ringgit was range bound but with a bias on the downside on back of selling pressure from overseas funds.
Dealers said the selling in the thin market was exaggerating the impact on the ringgit.
Dealers in Singapore said American funds have interest to buy dollar/ringgit at the 2.5100/2.5090 level.
However, upside for dollar/ringgit would be limited at 2.5140/50 level because of demand for ringgit from Malaysia.
The Singapore dollar was firmer on the back of the weak dollar/yen.
Dealers said local corporations had interest to sell dollar/Sing at 1.4300 and the unit looked likely to test 1.4260.
"If 1.4260 breaks, than dollar/Sing would head towards 1.4200 where it should be supported as local corporates have interest to buy there," said a dealer.
The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar, moving within a narrow range of 2,429 to 2,430 in the morning and was likely to remain so for the rest of the day, dealers said.
Liquidity was ample, with overnight money trading at 9.0/10.0 percent, but there was no dollar buying momentum seen in the market.
Dealers said strong rupiah resistance at the 2,430.0 level capped the upside, but the downside was also limited after Indonesia's general elections late last month.
Dealers said there was anticipation that the rupiah might head towards the low end of the central bank's intervention band once post-election fears of possible violence diminishes.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik
